timed_text.text: Day 30. You made it. Most people quit at Day 8 or 15 — you didn't.
You kept showing up every single day.
That is not a small thing.
Think about where you were when you started this.
No reset word, no If-Then plan, no evidence log, no traffic light system.
You have all of it now.
Not because someone gave it to you — you built it, rep by rep, day by day.
The question to carry from here: What's next?
Not how much did I improve, not was it worth it, what's next?
Take it into every season, every competition, every time you plateau.
Before you journal one last time, I want you to do one thing.
Open your visualization board. Look at who you committed to becoming.

cards.caption: Open your visualization board. The athlete you committed to becoming on Day 23. Take your time.
Now your evidence log. Read it from the beginning. Not to compare — to see.

cards.text: The distance between that board and where you stand right now? That's the work. And you've already started closing it.

timed_text.text: You don't need a score to know what's changed.
You know it in how you showed up, how you handled the last competition.
That's the evidence.
Keep the log, run the routine, use the tools, and build on your why.
When it gets hard, you've been here before and came out with a plan.
That's it.
Programs over, but your training isn't.
Go compete like it.

blocks.prompt: What is different about the way you think about competing now compared to where you started? What does the next chapter look like — and what's your first move?
